limitations_admitted.value: Outflow evidence is tentative and needs higher angular resolution and sensitivity

referee_caveats_inferred: Outflow inference rests on a single-beam spectrum with a broad wing; no uncertainty on chi-square significance and no test against a bulk-rotation or merger-shock origin beyond qualitative argument
M_dyn uses crude thin-disk geometry on a clearly disturbed merging system, so inclination and V_circ are poorly defined
SFR_[CII] and M_H2 from [CII] are calibrated on other populations and are not independent; the ~3-5x offset noted for other quasars is not applied
T_dust = 35 K is assumed, not fit, so L_TIR, M_dust and SFR_TIR are uncertain by factors of a few
The outflow mass assumes T_ex = 200 K, high-density limit and a 70% neutral fraction without sensitivity test
Aperture photometry choices (1.5'' vs 1.0'' diameter) are not tested for contamination between neighbouring components

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Two Band 6 execution blocks with 41 antennas, 106 min on source: raw data order of tens of GB; calibrated MS and cubes a few GB
reproducibility.score_reason: Data identified by project code and key settings (robust, CASA versions, calibrators, formulas, T_dust, beta, X_C+, T_ex) are given, and numerical results are listed, but line-free channel selection, image geometry, aperture centres and the dynamical-mass formula are not given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The archive links project 2019.A.00019.S to this paper (data availability itself not stated in the paper); the recipe is mostly given with numeric results in Table 1 and the text, but several imaging choices must be reconstructed.
